name: Next Kanban
description: Next Collection board that groups report rows into columns by Column Key, with counts, work-in-progress limits and moving cards by drag and drop or keyboard. Follows the column-board pattern of task tools, but the column header carries the load: every limit slot is drawn, so a full or overloaded column is visible before any card is read. Five styles, each for a named use: Calm lanes (smart, a procurement requisition pipeline; lanes stack when the region is narrow), Ops board (bold, a facilities work-order wallboard with large counts and priority codes), Sticky wall (depth, a campaign planning workshop of paper notes that lift when moved), Due timeline (motion, contract and licence renewals grouped by due date inside each column) and Compact list (smart, a field supervisor's phone view with one column per tab; drop a card on a tab to move it). The board never writes to the database: a move fires the amc:kanban-move event and can set page items for a Dynamic Action to save it.
helpText: One query row per card, already ordered by column and then by position (order by column_seq, card_seq). Map Card ID, Column Key, Column Label and Title; Column Limit (a number, the same on every row of the column) turns on the work-in-progress warning. To show an empty column, return one row for it with Card ID and Title empty. Due Date is ISO text, TO_CHAR(due_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Priority accepts critical, high, medium or low; State accepts success, warning, danger, info or neutral; Tags is a | separated list. When a card is moved the region fires the custom event amc:kanban-move with detail id, from, to, index (0-based position in the target column) and fromIndex, and first sets the page items named in Card Item, From Item, To Item and Index Item, so a Dynamic Action on that custom event can run a PL/SQL process that saves the move and then refreshes the region. Without JavaScript the rows show as a plain list.

attributes.name: Style
attributes.helpText: Design of the board; the direction is given in brackets as motion, depth, bold or smart. calmLanes [smart]: flat tinted lanes with quiet borderless cards and limit slots under each column name; the lanes stack when the region is narrow. opsBoard [bold]: a dense wallboard with large column counts, one-line cards and a solid priority code P1 to P4 (tags are not shown), and a column that goes over its limit turns red. stickyWall [depth]: paper notes tinted by priority, slightly turned, that lift off the wall while they are moved. dueTimeline [motion]: cards inside each column are ordered and grouped by Due Date into Overdue, Today, This week, Later and No date, and overdue dates pulse gently; moving up and down is off because the order comes from the date. compactList [smart]: one column at a time behind tabs with counts, for phones and narrow side regions; drop a card on a tab to move it there.

attributes.name: Card ID
attributes.helpText: Primary key of the card, returned as id in the amc:kanban-move event and put in Card Item. Leave it empty (with Title empty) on a row that only makes an empty column visible.

attributes.name: Column Key
attributes.helpText: Code of the column the card is in, for example REQUESTED or IN_REVIEW. Rows with the same key form one column; columns appear in the order their first row arrives. Returned as from and to in the amc:kanban-move event.

attributes.name: Column Label
attributes.helpText: Column name shown in the header, for example In review. The first row of each column provides it.

attributes.name: Column Limit
attributes.helpText: Work-in-progress limit of the column as a whole number, for example 4. The header draws one slot per allowed card, says At limit when full and Over limit by N when exceeded. Empty or 0 means no limit.

attributes.name: Title
attributes.helpText: Card heading, for example PR-2291 Laptops for the Dammam branch.

attributes.name: Description
attributes.helpText: Optional one or two lines of detail. Ops board and Compact list show one line.

attributes.name: Assignee
attributes.helpText: Name of the person who owns the card, for example Maha Alharbi.

attributes.name: Initials
attributes.helpText: One or two letters shown in the assignee disc, for example MA.

attributes.name: Due Date
attributes.helpText: Due date as ISO text, TO_CHAR(due_on, 'YYYY-MM-DD'). It is shown in the page language and marked Overdue or Due today; Due timeline groups cards by it.

attributes.name: Priority
attributes.helpText: critical, high, medium or low. Critical and high are shown as Urgent and High; medium and low stay quiet except in Ops board (P1 to P4) and Sticky wall (note tint). Other values render as medium.

attributes.name: Tags
attributes.helpText: Short labels separated by |, for example Riyadh|IT hardware. Keep to two or three.

attributes.name: State
attributes.helpText: Health of the card: success (Done), warning (At risk), danger (Blocked), info (Waiting on others) or neutral (no label). Always shown as text, never by color alone. Unknown values render as neutral.

attributes.name: Link URL
attributes.helpText: Optional page URL that opens the card, built in SQL with apex_page.get_url. The title becomes the link.

attributes.name: Allow Moving
attributes.helpText: Yes lets users move cards by dragging or with the Move button and arrow keys. No shows a read-only board.

attributes.name: Card Item
attributes.helpText: Name of a page item, for example P10_CARD_ID, that receives the moved card's ID before amc:kanban-move fires. Use a hidden item and submit it from the Dynamic Action.

attributes.name: From Item
attributes.helpText: Name of a page item that receives the Column Key the card left, for example P10_FROM_COLUMN.

attributes.name: To Item
attributes.helpText: Name of a page item that receives the Column Key the card was moved to, for example P10_TO_COLUMN.

attributes.name: Index Item
attributes.helpText: Name of a page item that receives the new 0-based position of the card in its column, for example P10_POSITION.
